title: National Health Mission: ASHA Handbook on Maternal Danger Signs and Emergency Referral Protocols
organization: National Health Mission (NHM), Govt of India

sections.content: Immediate danger signs requiring emergency medical care: 1) Vaginal bleeding at any time in pregnancy; 2) Severe, persistent headache with visual disturbances/blurriness; 3) Convulsions or sudden loss of consciousness; 4) High fever with chills or foul-smelling vaginal discharge; 5) Severe abdominal pain or rigid abdomen; 6) Leaking of amniotic fluid before onset of labor; 7) Reduced or absent fetal kicks (< 10 movements over 2 hours after a meal); 8) Extreme breathlessness at rest.

Emergency referral protocol for ASHA workers: 1) Immediately reassure the mother and family; 2) Dial 108 Emergency Ambulance service immediately for critical signs (convulsions, severe bleeding, obstructed labor); 3) For non-critical transport, arrange 102 Janani Express; 4) Prepare Maternal and Child Protection (MCP) card and referral slip with noted vital signs; 5) Inform the destination First Referral Unit (FRU) or PHC casualty in advance; 6) Accompany the pregnant woman to the hospital if possible; 7) Document referral time and track receiving facility admission.

sections.topic: Essential Tasks During ASHA Home Visits
sections.content: During an antenatal home visit, the ASHA must: 1) Inquire about mother's general well-being and screen for any danger signs; 2) Verify regular intake of IFA and Calcium tablets; 3) Check dietary intake (extra calorie requirement, iron-rich green leafy vegetables, proteins, safe water); 4) Guide birth preparedness (identifying delivery facility, transport arrangements, saving money, identifying blood donor); 5) Encourage institutional delivery and explain JSY / PMMVY financial entitlements; 6) Check next scheduled ANC date and remind family.
